title: 育儿与教育：四本书里的前沿研究 — Day 29
title_en: Parenting & Education: Frontier Research in Four Books — Day 29

questions.question: 一个孩子学了两年钢琴后说想换别的。按 Range 的思路，家长首先该弄清什么？
options: 孩子是真的不喜欢钢琴了，还是练到难处想躲开
新兴趣是否比钢琴更有利于升学，有利才同意换
两年的投入是否已经足够多，够多了就不该浪费
孩子是否已经错过了专精的最佳年龄，再换就来不及
questions.explanation: Epstein 主张在规则多变的领域广泛采样有价值，但他也提醒「广泛采样」不等于「一遇困难就换」。所以关键是分辨换方向还是躲困难，两者处理方式不同；把 Range 当成随时可以放弃的挡箭牌是常见误读。
questions.question_en: After two years of piano, a child says they want to try something else. Following the logic of Range, what should the parent figure out first?
options_en: Whether piano itself has lost its appeal or the child is dodging a hard stretch—the first is exploration, the second is avoidance
Whether the new interest helps more with school admissions, and only agree if it does
Whether two years is already a big enough investment that switching would waste it
Whether the child has already missed the best age to specialize, making a switch too late
questions.explanation_en: Epstein argues broad sampling pays off in fast-changing domains, but sampling is not the same as quitting at the first difficulty. The key is telling a change of direction from an escape from difficulty, because each calls for a different response; using Range as a license to quit is a common misreading.

questions.question: 关于「一万小时定律」，下面哪种说法最符合原始研究者的立场？
options: 一万小时是精确门槛，少一点都不行，多了则收益递减
Ericsson 证明了任何领域只要练满一万小时，都能达到专家水平
这是对 Ericsson 的简化，关键是刻意练习的质量而非时长
练习时长与水平无关，成就主要由天赋决定
questions.explanation: Gladwell 把 Ericsson 的研究压缩成「练满一万小时就能成」，Ericsson 本人公开反对：关键是刻意练习的质量，而且并非所有领域都适用。走到另一极端说练习与水平无关，同样不是原研究的结论。
questions.question_en: Which statement about the '10,000-hour rule' best reflects the position of the original researcher?
options_en: 10,000 hours is a precise threshold—any less won't do, and beyond it returns diminish
Ericsson showed that 10,000 hours of practice in any field produces expert-level performance
It oversimplifies Ericsson's research: what determines skill is the quality of deliberate practice, not the sheer pile of hours
Practice time has nothing to do with skill; achievement comes mainly from innate talent
questions.explanation_en: Gladwell condensed Ericsson's work into 'put in 10,000 hours and you'll make it,' and Ericsson publicly objected: the quality of deliberate practice is what matters, and the pattern does not hold in every field. Swinging to 'practice doesn't matter' is not his conclusion either.

questions.question: 孩子卡在一道难题前想放弃。按非认知能力研究的思路，哪种做法最能培养孩子的抗挫力？
options: 把题拆成小步，让孩子先做第一步，大人在旁边撑着
讲道理强调「坚持就是胜利」，让孩子明白毅力的重要
刻意多给孩子吃苦，用长期高压磨练韧性
先让孩子在坚毅量表上打分，找出短板再针对性训练
questions.explanation: 品格是在安全关系和「有人撑着熬过这一次难」的体验里长出来的，不是靠说教；长期高压不练韧性，只会损伤调节系统。把坚毅变成考核指标还会制造羞耻，而且 grit 的预测力经元分析并不比尽责性更强。
questions.question_en: A child is stuck on a hard problem and wants to give up. Following research on non-cognitive skills, which approach best builds resilience?
options_en: Break the problem into small steps, let the child try the first one, and stay nearby for support
Lecture that 'perseverance wins' so the child understands why grit matters
Deliberately give the child more hardship, using sustained pressure to toughen them up
Have the child score themselves on a grit scale first, then train the weak spots
questions.explanation_en: Character grows out of secure relationships and the experience of getting through a hard moment with someone backing you up—not out of lectures. Chronic pressure damages the stress-regulation system rather than building toughness, and turning grit into a metric breeds shame; meta-analyses also show grit predicts achievement no better than conscientiousness.
